verdict: Charter's revenue rose 9% to $14.9B as Cox joined the books, but a $6.3B write-down of its cable franchises swung it to a $2.4B loss for shareholders.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: actual basis, $14,922M vs $13,672M; pro forma (Cox owned all quarter both years) revenue fell 1.5%

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted loss per share attributable to Charter shareholders, vs +$8.34 a year ago

kpis.label: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.note: up 6.9% on an actual basis — the company's preferred cash-profit measure

kpis.label: Franchise impairment
kpis.note: non-cash write-down of cable franchise rights — the cause of the loss

segments.name: Residential
segments.note: Homes: Internet $6,395M, video $3,292M, mobile service $1,134M and voice $340M. Up 4.8% on an actual basis, helped by Cox; on a pro forma basis residential revenue fell 4.1%.

segments.name: Commercial
segments.note: Services to small businesses and larger companies, including the legacy Cox business customer base added in August. Up 22.6% on an actual basis.

segments.name: Advertising sales
segments.note: Selling advertising on its networks and platforms. Up 29.2%, helped by political advertising.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Mainly mobile device sales and other smaller revenue lines. Up 26.0%.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: A non-cash charge spreading the cost of the cable network, equipment and acquired customer relationships over their lives.

opex.name: Impairment of franchises
opex.note: A one-time, non-cash write-down of the value of Charter's cable franchise rights — see one-time items.

opex.name: Other operating expenses
opex.note: Other operating expenses, net of smaller items.

otherDetail: Other income, net was +$24M: other income of $1,365M — mainly a gain of about $1.4B on extinguishing debt in the Cox debt exchanges — almost fully offset by $1,341M of net interest expense.
oneTimers: Charter booked a $6,326M non-cash impairment of its cable franchises in the quarter — by far the largest item in these results. Without it, the operating result would have been a profit of about $2.8B.
Other income includes a gain of about $1.4B on extinguishing debt, from the debt exchanges tied to the Cox Transactions.
The Cox Transactions closed on August 20, 2026, so actual results include Cox only from that date. Charter also recorded $76M of Cox transition (integration) expenses inside operating costs.
footerNote: Charter does not report a cost-of-revenue or gross-profit line; its reported operating costs and expenses ($9,156M) are shown as the direct-cost block so the chart follows the reported lines. Consolidated net loss was $2,699M; after $302M of loss attributable to noncontrolling interests, the loss attributable to Charter shareholders was $2,397M. Chart note: running costs including the $6,326M franchise impairment exceeded gross profit, so the chart draws the $2,699M net loss as a shortfall funded from the balance sheet, not from revenue.

takeaways.title: A write-down made the loss
takeaways.text: The $6,326M franchise impairment is a non-cash accounting charge — no money left the company — but it turned an operating business that produced $5,943M of Adjusted EBITDA into a $3,526M operating loss and a $2,397M net loss for shareholders.

takeaways.title: Underneath Cox, sales shrank
takeaways.text: Actual revenue rose 9.1% only because Cox was added on August 20. Pro forma — Cox counted for the full quarter in both years — revenue fell 1.5% to $16,505M, as video and Internet revenue declined, partly offset by mobile service revenue up 17.3%.

takeaways.title: Mobile keeps growing, Internet slips
takeaways.text: On a pro forma basis Charter added 508,000 Spectrum Mobile lines in the quarter (13.5M in total) but lost 233,000 Internet customers (34.3M in total) and 77,000 video customers. Capex was $3,027M on an actual basis.
